name: Nota
comment: TextMate grammar for the Nota document language. Markup is the OUTER context (the inverse of JSX): a .nota file is markup at the top level, with JS embedded inside [props], @(expr), and %/%%% blocks (each delegated to source.ts). See design/notation.md for the full sigil inventory. TextMate is regex-only and cannot count balanced braces or track word boundaries across the document, so some constructs (intra-word emphasis, |@ re-arm, exact brace nesting) are best-effort here. The reader-faithful layer is the reader's highlight pass (Parser::parse_nota_highlights, an AST walk + embedded-JS re-lex in oxc_parser itself; the playground editor consumes it via wasm, and a future LSP semantic-tokens provider can serve the same spans in VSCode) -- this grammar remains the instant, server-independent base layer.

markup.comment: The top-level / body markup context. Order matters: TextMate is first-match, so escapes precede sigils, line-leading constructs precede inline ones, and raw spans (code/math/verbatim) precede emphasis and @-interpolation.

escape.comment: Backslash escapes for the documented set (\@ \{ \} \| \$ \* \_ \: \[ \] \` and \\), plus \# \- \+ \% for the line-leading sugar and \< \& for the R20a doc-state sugar (\[ already covers the footnote open). A backslash before any other char is literal text, so we only scope the known set.
escape.name: constant.character.escape.nota

fence-statement.comment: %%% ... %%% fence holds a raw JS block (embedded source.ts). Each fence is on its own line. We require the opening %%% to be alone on its line and end at a %%% alone on its line.
fence-statement.name: meta.embedded.block.statement.nota

line-statement.comment: % as first non-whitespace on a line begins a JS statement (the rest of the line; embedded source.ts). The sigil binds tight -- `%let`/`%const`/`%import` are valid with no space (the reader accepts it; the canonical golden uses `%let`), so we match a line-leading % NOT followed by another %, which excludes %%% (the fence, handled above) and %%. 50% is unaffected (not line-leading); \% forces a literal.
line-statement.name: meta.embedded.line.statement.nota

heading.comment: A line opening with 1-6 # followed by a space -> @h{n}. Body is the rest of the line and nests markup.
heading.name: markup.heading.nota

list.comment: List item markers at line start: -· (bullet -> ul), +· (number -> ol), N.· (alternate ol). The marker is punctuation; the rest of the line is ordinary markup handled by the outer context.

patterns.comment: -· bullet -> @ul (unnumbered).
+· -> @ol (numbered).
N.· explicit ordered marker -> @ol (numbered); the written number is ignored at runtime.

control-flow.comment: Content control flow: @if (c) {...}, @for (bind of iter) {...}, with else / else if continuations. Heads (the (...) condition / iterator) are embedded source.ts. The trailing {...} body is matched by #body via the outer markup context. `else`/`else if` are contextual: they only continue a conditional as the next token after a closing } -- we approximate with a lookbehind on } with optional whitespace (no blank line). `for`/`if` keep their @, only else/else-if are sigil-less.

patterns.comment: @if / @for keyword + parenthesized head (embedded TS). The condition/iterator parens delegate to source.ts; `of` in @for is highlighted by source.ts as an operator.
patterns.name: meta.control.head.nota

patterns.comment: else if (d) {...} -- contextual continuation right after a closing }.
patterns.name: meta.control.head.nota

patterns.comment: else {...} -- contextual continuation right after a closing }.

paren-expr.comment: A parenthesized embedded-JS span: ( ... ) delegating to source.ts. Used for @if/@for heads and @(expr). Balanced inner parens are tracked by re-including source.ts, which itself opens/closes nested () groups; the outer end matches the final ). Nested () balancing is best-effort (TextMate cannot truly count), but source.ts's own (..) rule absorbs nested pairs in practice.
paren-expr.name: meta.embedded.expression.nota

element.comment: The @-form heads. Ordered most-specific first: dynamic @(expr) tag, then Capitalized component, then lowercase host. Each head is just the sigil + name/parens; the optional [props] and {body} that follow are picked up by #props and #body in the surrounding markup context (TextMate cannot reliably balance the braces in a single begin/end, so we tokenize the head and let the generic block rules handle the body -- the same factoring the Typst grammar uses for #func then (...) / [...]).

patterns.comment: Dynamic tag head: @(expr) used AS A TAG, i.e. immediately followed by [ or {. The expr is embedded source.ts.
patterns.name: meta.tag.dynamic.nota

patterns.comment: Capitalized component head: @Cap{ / @Cap[ / @Cap: / @Cap|{ -- an element only when followed by an element trigger ({ [ : or a |{ verbatim body). A bare @Cap with no trigger is interpolation (handled by #interpolation), so we require the trigger via lookahead. The : (colon sugar) is captured; { [ and |{ are left for #body / #props / #verbatim.

Lowercase host element head: @tag{ / @tag[ / @tag: / @tag|{ -- an element only when followed by a trigger ({ [ : or a |{ verbatim body, e.g. @code|{...}|). A bare @tag with no trigger is interpolation. \@foo\: is a literal colon (handled by #escape on \:).

doc-state.comment: The R20 doc-state inline sugars, each a rewrite to an element form: `<ident>` -> @Label[id], `&ident` -> @Ref[id], `[^ident]` -> @FootnoteMark[label], and line-start `[^ident]: body` -> @FootnoteText[label]: body. Ident charset (R20 re-amended 2026-07-05 -- Typst minus period; supersedes the brief JS-IdentifierName amendment): start `[A-Za-z0-9_]`, continue `[A-Za-z0-9_:-]`, ASCII-only. Digits may start a label (`[^1]`, Markdown-style; `<1>` also fires); kebab labels work (`<sec-intro>`, `&sec-intro`); the colon is a continue char (`<sec:i>`); period is NOT in the set, so `&sec.` reads the ident as `sec` and leaves the `.` literal. `<` and `&` carry a LEFT-BOUNDARY GUARD -- they fire only at start-of-body/line or after whitespace / opening punctuation ( [ { " ' -- so Vec<T>, R&D, a<b, a&b stay literal prose; the guard is a fixed-width negative lookbehind `(?<![^\s(\[{"'])` (no preceding char, i.e. line/body start, also passes). The start restriction keeps arrow-like prose literal (`<->`, `<-x>` -- `-` is not a valid start char). `[^` needs no guard (the digraph is unambiguous and glues after a word, Markdown-style). Escapes \< \& \[ (handled by #escape, which runs first) force literals. Ordered definition-before-mark so a line-start `[^x]:` is the multi-arg definition, not a mark plus stray colon.

patterns.comment: Line-start footnote DEFINITION `[^ident]: body` -> @FootnoteText[label]: body. The `]:` closes the head; the rest of the line is the colon-sugar body, left to the outer markup context (so nested @em{...}/@name in it still highlight).
Footnote REFERENCE `[^ident]` -> @FootnoteMark[label]. No boundary guard (glues after a word like Markdown; digit-start `[^1]` fires, Markdown-style).

Label ANCHOR `<ident>` -> @Label[id]. Boundary-guarded on `<`; must close with `>` on the opening line. Kebab `<sec-intro>` and colon `<sec:i>` fire (the `-`/`:` are continue chars); the start restriction keeps arrow-like prose literal (`<->`, `<-x>`, `< b` — `-`/space is not a valid start char). Vec<T> stays literal via the left-boundary guard.

Cross-REFERENCE `&ident` -> @Ref[id]. Boundary-guarded on `&`; ends at the first non-ident char (so R&D and `a&b` stay literal). Kebab `&sec-intro` fires (the `-` is a continue char); `&sec.` reads the ident as `sec` with the `.` left literal (period is NOT in the charset -- Typst minus period).

interpolation.comment: Bare @name identifier interpolation -> {name}. Only matches when NOT followed by { [ : ( (those are element triggers handled by #element). A bare identifier only (no member access at the @name form; @(expr) covers member access).

props.comment: [k:v, ...] prop list: object-literal-ish, embedded JS. Delegates to source.ts so keys, string/expression values, shorthand, and spreads highlight. A value may itself be markup (@em{..}); since source.ts does not know @-forms, markup-valued props are best-effort (the @ head will look like a stray token to TS highlighting, but the bracket structure is preserved). The reader highlight pass (Parser::parse_nota_highlights) classifies markup-valued props faithfully; over LSP that refinement lands with the semantic-tokens provider.
props.name: meta.props.nota

props-colon.comment: R21: `@head[props]: body` -- a colon glued to a [props] group's closing `]` is the same colon-sugar element trigger as a bare `@head:` (identical R12 gate + colon-body extent, props threaded through). #props consumes the `[...]` and returns; this scopes the immediately-following `:` (the body is the rest of the line, handled by the outer markup context, so nested @em{...}/@name still highlight). Lookbehind-anchored on the props close `]` so a bare prose colon never matches; TextMate cannot check that the `]` actually closed an element's props (best-effort, like the rest of this grammar -- the reader highlight pass is faithful).

body.comment: A { ... } body block: recursively the markup context. This also matches the @{...} fragment body (the @ is consumed by nothing special; bare @{ has its @ fall through to #interpolation's negative lookahead, leaving the { to open here). Brace NESTING is handled by re-entry: an inner { opens a nested #body. Unbalanced braces in prose should be escaped (\{ \}).
body.name: meta.body.nota

bold.comment: *...* -> markup.bold (@strong). Word-boundary: opens only at a left word boundary, closes only at a right one, so intra-word * stays literal. Best-effort via lookarounds (TextMate cannot do true Unicode word segmentation). Ends at a line break too. Body nests markup.
bold.name: markup.bold.nota

italic.comment: _..._ -> markup.italic (@em). Same word-boundary rule as bold, so my_var_name stays literal.
italic.name: markup.italic.nota

verbatim.comment: |{ ... }| raw body: sigils off, braces literal, ends at }|. No embedded scopes. The armed escape |@ re-enters Nota to produce element children -- best-effort: we scope |@ as a re-arm punctuation but do NOT actually switch back to markup highlighting (a TextMate limitation; the reader highlight pass classifies the re-armed form faithfully).
verbatim.name: markup.raw.verbatim.nota string.unquoted.verbatim.nota

patterns.comment: |@ re-arm marker (best-effort scope only).
patterns.name: punctuation.definition.verbatim.rearm.nota keyword.control.rearm.nota

code-block.comment: ```lang\n ... \n``` fenced code, optional language tag on the opening line. Raw (String.raw). When the language is one we ship a grammar for, the content is embedded as source.{lang}; otherwise it stays raw markup. Backtick runs shorter than the closing fence are literal inside. Each rule matches a >=3 backtick fence and closes on the same run length via the \1 backreference. Language-specific rules come first; the generic raw fence is the fallback.

patterns.comment: TypeScript-tagged fence -> embed source.ts.
patterns.name: markup.raw.code.block.nota

patterns.comment: JavaScript-tagged fence -> embed source.js.
patterns.name: markup.raw.code.block.nota

patterns.comment: JSON-tagged fence -> embed source.json.
patterns.name: markup.raw.code.block.nota

patterns.comment: Generic fence: any other language tag, or none. Stays raw (the at-minimum scoping required by Phase U). The language tag, if present, is still captured for theming.
patterns.name: markup.raw.code.block.nota

code-inline.comment: `...` inline code -> CodeInline. Raw (String.raw). Backtick runs shorter than the closing fence are literal. We match a run of 1+ backticks and close on the same length.
code-inline.name: markup.raw.code.inline.nota string.unquoted.code.nota

math-display.comment: $$ ... $$ display math -> <Math display>. Content is raw LaTeX (String.raw); @ interpolates a string value; \$ / \@ are literal (the backslash is kept). Must precede inline math so $$ is not read as two empty $...$.
math-display.name: markup.math.display.nota string.other.math.nota

math-content.comment: Inside math: \$ and \@ are literal LaTeX escapes (backslash kept); @name / @(expr) interpolate a string value.

patterns.comment: @(expr) interpolation inside math (embedded TS).

@name interpolation inside math. The identifier must NOT include $ (the math delimiter), so a closing $ right after the name -- $a_@i$ -- still ends the math rather than being eaten as an identifier char.
